text: The rule-change request is a record of rwb-access and not a table of rwb-access: one entry of the local decision-record chain of the DP-03 library, written with an idempotency row in the same transaction, with the rule package version consumed through the P7 contract and its fake. The missing RWB-P7 rule-package contract dependency is raised at D1 and is not added to the metadata of this story.
why: The rule registry, its versions and its rows are P7's under ASM-A6-tables-3 and ASM-A6-api-3, so this service can neither hold the version nor read a rule table, while an administrative decision that is not recorded cannot be defended; the sources name no table and no operation for the change request itself.
read: TSD P4 v3 T6.3 and T4; Temporal and Drools design slide 15 (governance central in rwb-decision); ownership map rows rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case and the rule-package API paths (ASM-A6-tables-3, ASM-A6-api-3); DP-01 and DP-03.
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-decision and the tech lead of rwb-access
impact: A cross-service change record needs a registry table or a central record instead of the local chain, and the audit consumer would read P7 rather than rwb-access.

text: The seven items of TSD P4 v3 T6.3 — request, impact, test result, approver, load, verify and rollback plan — are the change checklist of the change request, checked for completeness when the change is raised and carried as the seven required item codes of the RuleChangeChecklist schema; a missing item is refused 422 with MSG-P3-022 naming the item code.
why: The technical specification attaches the checklist to the approval of a version and names no check at the point where the change is raised, and this story must refuse an incomplete change before any registry hop so the analyst learns the missing item while the change is still only a form.
read: TSD P4 v3 T6.3 (change_checklist, DF-REF-295, MSG-P3-022); FSD P4 v3 A2.18; the message table of the rule-change stories for the text of MSG-P3-022; the pattern list of the key holds no DP07 and the contract-dependency list no RWB-P3-E1043-CON, so the item codes are contract constants rather than a reference-data read.
confirm: Centre of excellence and the internal audit representative
impact: If the checklist belongs only to the approval, the change request carries the items as reference and the registry remains the only gate; the 422 of an incomplete change would then become a warning and no change would be refused here.

text: The record code of an administrative change is the administrative-change code of the local decision-record library, and the change entry is written under it with the change id in the reference field of the entry; the change id is minted by this service and is opaque to every consumer.
why: The sources fix the decision codes of a case decision and of an access event and give no code for an administrative change, and the entry must be findable by the identifier the screen and the audit quote.
read: TSD P4 v3 T6.3 (a change log entry is append only, with the version label, the status change, the author or approver and the time); LDM v8 DF-DEC-003 for the decision code and DF-DEC-008 for the reference field; DP-03 for the local library.
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-access and the owner of the decision-record library
impact: A different record code changes the value written on every change entry and the filter the audit consumer uses; the entry would still be found by its change id.
